why: Config guards are not exercised by the suite record: replay re-derives step verdicts from recorded rates and never constructs a Cfg. Two config guards were merged without being checked against these, and one of them (the VM budget rule in #68) refused configurations that had already produced accepted runs -- it capped the broker at 3,613m while the broker guard's own hint asked for 5,632m, so on that host the two guards had no configuration in common, and run 22 produced no step ratios at all. Every entry here is a configuration whose verdict we already know; a guard that disagrees with one is wrong.

configs.name: run 21 (accepted, 2->4 = 1.865x, over-committed broker on a 7.8 GB VM)
runs 13-19 (flat worker memory: refused on purpose since #62)
configs.why: a flat figure divides across each case's subtasks, so the 4-core case ran on a quarter of what each 2-core subtask had

configs.name: six partitions with a four-core case (refused since #57)
configs.why: 2/2/1/1 per subtask, so the busiest subtask sets the pace and the case cannot reach its cap
